pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic School Inspection - Sacred Heart Primary School Whetstone
pageCache.text:
Catholic School Inspection
Sacred Heart Primary school was inspected by the Catholic Schools Inspectorate in February 2026 and was rated as Outstanding in all areas.
The report highlights:
The strong sense of welcome reflects a community in which the mission statement is clearly understood and consistently lived out by pupils, staff and families.
Pupils feel safe, happy and secure
Behaviour is exemplary, pupils consistently model kindness, respect and responsibility.
Parents are key partners in this vibrant prayer life and are regularly invited to participate in assemblies, liturgies and celebrations, fostering a strong sense of shared faith and community.
Staff feel genuinely valued and well supported in their physical and mental wellbeing, as well as in their professional development.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome
Welcome to Sacred Heart Primary School. We are a two form of entry voluntary aided Catholic Primary School situated in the London borough of Barnet, within the Diocese of Westminster. There are over 400 children and more than 60 staff here who are all "Learning together in God's Love".
We aim to give all our children a great start in life by fostering a love of learning and a desire to be the best they can in whatever they do. We pride ourselves on building good relationships with families from the moment your child is offered a place with us , as we know that working in partnership with parents and carers leads to happy pupils who are ready to learn.
At Sacred Heart we achieve excellent results through setting high expectations for all pupils and supporting them to achieve. We encourage our pupils to collaborate and work together to support each other in their learning. We set high standards for behaviour and encourage children to reach these standards through praise and rewards.
We welcome visits to the school, which can be arranged by contacting the school office at office@sacredheart.barnetmail.net or by telephone on 020 8445 3854.
Our Latest OFSTED report can be found below in the documents section.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Life and Mission - Sacred Heart Primary School Whetstone
pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
Catholic Life and Mission
Sacred Heart RC Primary School
We are preparing our children to be saints - the people that God created them to be - by ensuring that we provide them with an outstanding education and offer them a wealth of opportunities and experiences to enable them to become good, happy people and have “fullness of life” (John 10:10).
Sacred Heart is a Catholic Primary School where we serve the Catholic community of Whetstone. We welcome children and staff of all faiths where we celebrate and learn from one another. We follow our mission statement of ‘Learning together in God’s love.'
Inspired by Christian values, we aim to provide love and security within a curriculum designed to meet the needs of all individuals, in order to prepare them to take place in the ever changing world of today and tomorrow.
We want our learners to learn the essential knowledge and skills which help them to form positive, caring and loving relationships with all children and adults within the school community, while loving the process of learning.
Religious Education is the core subject in the curriculum and provides our pupils the chance to deepen their relationship with God As a Catholic School, we devote 10% of curriculum time to the teaching of Religious Education; this is separate from times of prayer and collective worship, liturgies and class prayer, which happen in addition to the taught curriculum. The aim is to help promote knowledge and understanding of catholic faith and life. It also allows them to develop an awareness and understanding of how their faith impacts their daily life. By learning about the catholic religion as well as others, we hope to foster attitudes of respect towards all who live in our society. Throughout their time here, pupils will have the opportunity to learn about Sikhism, Islam, Hinduism and Judaism.
We aim to be a welcoming school and part of the wider community. We have strong links with our parish church, and our children visit our church regularly. We encourage our children to care of God's world and its people by developing empathy, sympathy and a need to live their faith through charitable works. Our Mini Vinnies are a group of KS2 children who work together to support our local and wider community. As a school, we fundraise for different charities such as McMillian Cancer research, CAFOD as well as local charities.
Our pupils support wider initiatives such as Just One Tree day where money is raised to plant a million trees in Poland and Europe and beyond to help climate change. We encourage the pupils to take an active role in their future but teaching them how to love and care and respect all things around us.
It is our aim that children leave Sacred Heart School as resilient, respectful, confident, thoughtful and independent young people, prepared for the next stage on their journey towards leading a fulfilled life in the presence of God.
"Start children off on the way they should go, and even when they are old they will not turn from it." - Proverbs 22:6

pageCache.text:
Prayer and Worship at Sacred Heart
Prayer and worship is central to Catholic Life at Sacred Heart. Our pupils are supported on their spiritual journey through access to wide range of opportunities for prayer and worship.
These range from opportunities for quiet prayer alone to classroom based prayers, to whole school celebration of the word assemblies, pupil led assemblies and other services including mass and the sacrament of reconciliation.
Our pupils experience these opportunities both in school and at the school’s parish church, Mary Magdalen Church. We also support prayer at home by sharing resources and ideas with parents.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Social Teaching - Sacred Heart Primary School Whetstone
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
At Sacred Heart we incorporate Catholic Social Teaching in all aspects of school life: through the whole curriculum, through the Catholic Life and Mission of the school and through prayer and worship and the liturgical calendar. This makes these teachings meaningful and memorable for our pupils and ensures that they understand how we can live out our Catholic beliefs in the world.
We focus on a specific Catholic Social Teaching principle each half term:
Autumn 1 - Care for Creation
Autumn 2 - Preferential Option for the Poor
Spring 1 - Solidarity and Peace
Spring 2 - Community and Participation
Summer 1 - Dignity of the worker
We use the Cafod animal characters to support our pupils to remember and understand how these principles guide us to live according to our faith.

Our Church
St Mary Magdalen is our school parish church. We work closely with the Parish for the benefit of our pupils, their families and the community.
Our parish priest is Fr John and he is very involved in the catholic life of our school.
Father John likes to visit our school and support us in prayer. He leads Christian meditation sessions with children in KS2 and for parents in our school community.
He will come into school to lead important masses throughout the year and we always like attending masses and reconciliation services at St Mary Magdalen Church.
Please see a link to our school parish church.

Links To Other Curriculum Subjects
Design and Technology
We took part in a very special International and DT week at Sacred Heart linked to our Jubilee Year of hope.
We remember it is a special period of forgiveness and reconciliation, celebrated every 25 years. The late Pope Francis declared it a Jubilee Year of Hope. It is a sacred time of renewal, reflection and grace.
On Monday 19th to Friday 22nd May 2025 we linked pilgrimages from around the world and the traditional foods that people would take with them on this journey.
These are the pilgrimages that each year group learnt about:
On Friday 22nd May we got to showcase all our wonderful projects and it provided a lovely link with DT. Some children from each class taught us all about the pilgrimage that they had learnt about. There was lots of lovely work on show in each class and the children were very proud of all their work they had done over this special week.
FS – Knock Shrine in Ireland
Year 2 – Lourdes in France
Year 3 – The Vatican in Italy
Year 4 – Jerusalem in Israel
Year 5 – Fatima in Portugal

pageCache.text:
Personal Development
Personal Development Opportunities
Sacred Heart place personal development and wellbeing at the heart of the school’s vision, ensuring that pupils develop into confident, respectful, resilient and responsible individuals who are well prepared for life in modern Britain. The school’s PSHE provision is designed to promote pupils’ emotional wellbeing, character, safety, and understanding of relationships, alongside strong moral, social, spiritual and cultural development.
The school aims to ensure that all pupils, including the most vulnerable, feel safe, valued and supported, and that they are taught the skills needed to manage emotions, build positive relationships and contribute positively to the school community. Personal development provision is inclusive, proactive and responsive to pupils’ needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors - Sacred Heart Primary School Whetstone
pageCache.text:
Governors
Welcome from the Chair of Governors
Welcome to the Governors’ section of the site where you can find out more about the Governors and the work that we do.
Our team of dedicated Governors draw on their various backgrounds and experience to provide strategic support to the Head Teacher and the school. We are committed to making sure that the school’s performance is evaluated and continuously improves, to provide strategic direction for the school, to ensure legal obligations are met and that the school keeps abreast of whatever challenges are thrown its way. Most of all, we are here because we care for our school and its community and want it to succeed.
Our aim is to ensure Sacred Heart Primary School provides its pupils the best educational start in life in a happy, safe and caring environment, helping them to become confident individuals who are given every opportunity to reach their potential.
We hope you will find the website useful. We welcome feedback and ideas on how we can improve.
Who we are
Tony McMahon - Chair of Governors and Safeguarding Governor
I am the deputy head of a Primary school in King’s Cross and have been there since I was newly qualified thirteen years ago. I am from Islington but moved to Whetstone with my wife and son in 2019 and my child now attends Sacred Heart. I have taught in a wide range of year groups in my time.
Chris Sheils - Vice Chair of Governors
I am a secondary school teacher based in a Catholic school in St Albans, specialising in History and Politics. I previously worked in the London Borough of Brent. My current role is as Deputy Head of Sixth Form, where I focus on a wide range of areas such as student attainment, pastoral development, and safeguarding. Prior to training as a teacher I worked in politics, where I was part of the clerking team for the education select committee in the Northern Ireland Assembly. I am a former pupil at Sacred Heart, and have been a governor since 2020. I was appointed Chair of Governors in September 2023.
Alice Campbell - Foundation Governor
I work as Health and Safety consultant for Judicium Education. My role includes looking after Primary and Secondary schools where I complete H&S Audits, Fire Risk Assessments and deliver H&S training. This includes working closely with Headteachers, School Business Managers, Governors and Premises team. I am comfortable speaking and presenting different views in sometimes difficult situations. I care deeply about education, which is why I have chosen this career path. I am proud of being a part in helping Sacred Heart School maintain its existing high standards. I committed the time and energy in building relationships with the parents and represent their opinions. I consider myself to be a people person, very approachable whilst being sensitive with information. I have been a governor at the school since 2021 and became a foundation governor in October 2022. I believe I am a good governor bringing my passion, experience and knowledge to the school community.
Duncan Hamilton - Foundation Governor
I am now in my ninth year as a RE teacher at a local Catholic Secondary school, having attended it as a pupil. I currently have responsibility for overseeing the KS3 curriculum as second in department. I also have a daughter at Sacred Heart, and feel privileged to have this opportunity to support the development of the school as it continues to provide excellent opportunities for all of its students to learn, in an environment that has a strong Catholic ethos at its core.
Maria Casling Brown - Foundation Governor
I attended what was then called The Convent of the Sacred Heart School many years ago when I was a young girl. From 2001 - 2016 I worked as an administrator in the office at Sacred Heart and my son also attended the school. So I have experienced Sacred Heart as a student, a parent and staff!
I have worked as the head teacher's PA at a local, Barnet secondary school since 2016.
My Catholic faith is hugely important to me: I made my first holy communion, was confirmed and married at Our Lady of Lourdes parish, N11.
I hope to be able to contribute to the governing body board with my previous experience and faith guiding me.
Nia Panayiotopoulos- Local Authority Governor I have been a Local Authority Governor at Sacred Heart since September 2020 and love being a part of a diverse group of supportive and proactive Governors. I have worked in the Voluntary Sector and in schools in the London Borough of Barnet for over 20 years. I have supported small charities with developing policies and procedures. I was previously a Parent Governor at Brookhill Nursery School. I am a local resident and have three children all of whom attend Barnet schools. I am passionate about inclusion for all children and the need for strong pastoral care, especially after the pandemic. I am familiar with SEN support/services in Barnet and statutory responsibilities. This has led me to be the SEN Governor. I sit on the curriculum and welfare sub-committee and help with admissions.
John Desbois - Parent Governor
As a business owner and health and safety consultant, I bring a strong focus on wellbeing and practical safety to my role as a governor. I am passionate about the power of community and coach a local football team, where I encourage the physical and social benefits of sport. With experience in enterprise and work-related learning education, I am committed to helping students develop both academically and personally, fostering skills that will serve them throughout life.
Sofia Gradoni - Parent Governor
I work for the Institute of Education at UCL in the department of Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment. I am also a member of one of the EDI Advisory Boards there and am passionate about ensuring that everyone receives a welcoming and inclusive environment in which to flourish. I have previously worked in Private Banking and gained the qualifications necessary to provide investment advice. As a Parent Governor I intend to use the skills gained in these varied roles to continue the standards of excellence already set at the school and help contribute to the children's wellbeing, as well as their academic success.
Fr John McKenna - Parish Priest at St Mary Magdalen, Whetstone
Hello, my name is Fr John McKenna. I was ordained in 2006 as a priest for the Diocese of Westminster. I was previously parish priest at Mary Immaculate and St Gregory chuch in Barnet for eleven years and also a school governor at St Catherine's primary school in Barnet. I always enjoy visiting schools and am particularly fond of teaching children how to pray, focusing on Christian meditation.

Design and Technology
We took part in a very special International and DT week at Sacred Heart linked to our Jubilee Year of hope.
We remember it is a special period of forgiveness and reconciliation, celebrated every 25 years. The late Pope Francis declared it a Jubilee Year of Hope. It is a sacred time of renewal, reflection and grace.
On Monday 19th to Friday 22nd May 2025 we linked pilgrimages from around the world and the traditional foods that people would take with them on this journey.
These are the pilgrimages that each year group learnt about:
On Friday 22nd May we got to showcase all our wonderful projects and it provided a lovely link with DT. Some children from each class taught us all about the pilgrimage that they had learnt about. There was lots of lovely work on show in each class and the children were very proud of all their work they had done over this special week.

pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Activities
All year groups go on lots of different extra-curricular trips to support their learning. So far this year these have included: The Globe Theatre, The Science Museum, The RAF Museum, Verulamium, a tour around London as well as in-house workshops ranging from money workshops, heart dissections and a workshop about Florence Nightingale.
We also have whole school weeks on specific subjects. So far this year, children have had a Maths Day, Science Day, D&T week as well as celebrating Mental Health Day, Anti Bullying and Safer Internet Week.
Being able to offer our children a wide range of diverse extra curricular activities is very important as it encourages them to become independent, confident and successful members of the community. In school we offer:
Drama, Choir, Music, Rocksteady, Coding, French, Spanish, Chess, Netball, Football, Gymnastics, Art, well-being, Irish Dancing, Reading,Taekwondo, Dance and Homework Club
We have now transferred our after school wrap around care provision to Smart Play please contact them directly for details of how to register and book smart-play.co.uk/contact-us/ .
